title: Taskified Ops Recipes: lightweight admin microservice + scheduler for one-click remediations
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Goal: Build a small, composable admin microservice and task scheduler that turns existing runbook steps into idempotent, reviewable tasks that can be executed from Console or CLI. This ticket scopes the initial MVP: a Task API + lightweight scheduler + permissioned execution path with audit logging and simple templating for input variables.

Background: Our support team spends ~30% of oncall time copy/pasting procedural steps from Confluence into shell sessions. Existing runbooks are narrative and not machine-friendly. We want a platform-first approach: represent steps as tasks with typed inputs, optional safety gates, and telemetry hooks so we can: (1) reduce MTTR with one-click remediations, (2) run dry-runs in a sandbox, (3) tie executions to RBAC and KMS-backed credential access.

MVP scope:
- Task manifest format (YAML/JSON) that defines inputs, idempotency key, estimated cost, and human-readable instructions.
- Task execution microservice (stateless) exposing: POST /v1/tasks/:id/execute, GET /v1/executions/:id, and webhooks for completion.
- Scheduler that supports immediate, delayed, and scheduled (cron-lite) runs; minimal backoff and concurrency limit per-task.
- Console integration: action button to call Task API with a typed form; confirmation modal with safety gates.
- Audit trail: immutable execution log stored to central telemetry with request/response chunks, operator id, and links to related incidents.
- Security: integration with our existing credential broker for ephemeral secrets; require role "ops_executor" for production tasks.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Author a sample task for "Reconnect Redis node" with inputs and idempotency semantics.
2) Execute sample task from Console and see execution appear in audit log and telemetry dashboard.
3) Dry-run mode that validates inputs and returns a simulated trace without side effects.
4) RBAC enforced: user without ops_executor receives 403.
5) Scheduler can run a delayed job and mark completion/failed appropriately.

Non-goals (MVP): task language DSL, complex branching steps, full runbook import, multi-step orchestration (we will support single-step tasks with safe wrappers initially).

Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind "taskified-ops" gate. Start with internal beta for SRE/support, then open to platform-first customers under pilot agreements.

Monitoring & SLOs: success rate, mean execution latency, and mean side-effect time. Alerts for >5% failure rate over 15m window.

Notes on trade-offs:
- We could have built on top of existing runbook DSL, but that would require large refactor of narrative content. Opting for a new small manifest makes iteration faster.
- Execution microservice is stateless to simplify autoscaling; scheduler holds durable state to avoid correlating failures across services.
comments: 2025-02-11: Kickoff sync with SRE and Support. Agreement to start with single-step task model and rely on platform orchestration for complex flows.
2025-02-12: Design review notes from Maya (Design): prefer typed inputs and show most-recent successful run metadata in the Console action panel. Action: DES-203 to prototype UX mockups.

2025-02-13: Engineering spike completed: implemented prototype of Task manifest parser and an in-memory scheduler. Benchmarks: simple task execute path ~120ms cold, ~30ms warm for simulated steps. Spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1428

2025-02-15: Security review (initial): require credential broker integration for any task that uses secrets. Follow-up: draft threat model and list of sensitive task categories. (See Drive doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/ops/task-security-model)

2025-02-17: Blocker discovered: current credential broker library lacks token-exchange API for short-lived ops credentials. Proposal: add token exchange endpoint to cred-broker (ENG-100602). If blocked, we will continue with sandbox-only tasks for beta.

2025-02-18: PR opened for Task API scaffolding: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1459. Requesting review from @Liam and @Nora. Next: wire Console button and create sample task for Redis reconnection.
